SaaS Sellability Checklist
The $20M+ ARR edition. You are here

Read your SaaS the way a buyer reads it. Check the foundations buyers test at your size, score where you stand, and see what to strengthen before the next stage.

Buyers do not pay for what you built. They pay for what transfers. Let's look at your company through their eyes.
Buyer Lens
At $20M+ ARR, buyers value your company on an EBITDA multiple or revenue multiple with Rule of 40. Here is what they look at first.

Who Buys At This Size

  • Institutional PE
  • Public strategics
  • Large PE-backed platforms

Typical Deal Structure

Cash at close; management rollover; representations and warranties insurance

Multiples In Full

Revenue: No BVR band above $20M; use the $5M to $20M band as a floor and public comparables as a ceiling.

EBITDA: $5M to $20M band as a floor: 8.7x / 16.9x / 28.3x.

25th percentile / median / 75th percentile. Source: BVR exit transaction data as cited in the LIVMO SaaS Exit Valuation Guide.

Top Buyer Concerns At This Size

  • Audit quality
  • Leadership depth
  • Comparables
  • Integration risk

How The Multiple Moves

Growth, retention and transferability set where you land in the range. The 25th percentile and the 75th percentile are the same business with different answers to the items in this checklist.

Stage 1: Your Checklist You are here
Tick every box that is true today. Add the points at the end. Items worth 2 points are the ones buyers weight most.

Financial quality

9 items
Year-end financials prepared by a CPA, at the review level your size requires
Benchmark: Audited
Why buyers care. Third-party financials cut diligence time and remove the first reason a buyer discounts your numbers.
Strengthen. Engage a SaaS-experienced CPA; step up to review or audit as you grow.
1 pt
ARR, churn, and customer counts in your billing or CRM system reconcile to the P&L
Benchmark: Within 1%
Why buyers care. Buyers compare your metrics pack to your financials. A gap in either direction signals weak controls.
Strengthen. Reconcile billing system ARR to recognized revenue every quarter and document the differences.
2 pts
All tax filings are current and every dollar of revenue runs through the books
Benchmark: All filings current; no off-book revenue
Why buyers care. Buyers inherit tax exposure in a stock deal and discount it in an asset deal.
Strengthen. Bring payroll, sales tax, and income tax filings current; close any off-book channel.
1 pt
No cash-flow crisis in the past 24 months and at least 3 months of operating cash on hand
Benchmark: 6 months of cash
Why buyers care. Buyers read cash history as a test of management. A crisis in the trailing period raises the risk premium.
Strengthen. Hold a cash reserve and track runway monthly.
1 pt
A live financial dashboard tracks ARR, churn, cash, and margin by month
Benchmark: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history
Why buyers care. A dashboard that updates without you proves the business reports on itself.
Strengthen. Connect billing and accounting to one dashboard and review it monthly with your team.
1 pt
4

Financial quality, continued

A 12-month budget exists and last year's actuals landed within 10% of plan
Benchmark: Within 10% of plan
Why buyers care. Buyers pay for a forecast they can trust. A track record of hitting plan supports forward multiples.
Strengthen. Build an annual budget, compare monthly, and document variances.
1 pt
A Quality of Earnings report or QoE-style package is ready before you go to market
Benchmark: Sell-side QoE completed within the last 12 months
Why buyers care. Institutional buyers commission a QoE. A sell-side QoE finds problems before they do and shortens diligence.
Strengthen. Commission a sell-side QoE 6 to 12 months before a sale.
1 pt
Consistent historical financials cover the required number of years
Benchmark: 5 years
Why buyers care. Buyers want to see growth across multiple years, in one format, with no gaps.
Strengthen. Restate earlier years into the current chart of accounts if needed.
1 pt
Financial foundations are in place: accrual books, monthly close within 15 days, SaaS chart of accounts, monthly revenue recognition, deferred revenue tracked
Benchmark: All 5 foundations in place
Why buyers care. At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
Strengthen. Audit the basics with your CPA before you start a process.
1 pt

Revenue quality

8 items
Recurring revenue is the required share of total revenue
Benchmark: 90%+
Why buyers care. Recurring revenue is what buyers pay the SaaS multiple on. Services and one-time fees get a lower multiple or none.
Strengthen. Productize services into subscriptions and separate one-time revenue in your reporting.
1 pt
5

Revenue quality, continued

ARR growth, as a 2 to 3 year CAGR, meets the benchmark, and every year in that period grew
Benchmark: 15%+
Why buyers care. Growth is the largest single driver of the multiple. Buyers read a multi-year CAGR with steady years as proof of product-market fit; one strong year does not count.
Strengthen. Track ARR growth monthly by cohort and segment; fix retention before you add acquisition spend.
2 pts
Gross revenue retention (annual) meets the benchmark
Benchmark: 90%+
Why buyers care. GRR shows how much revenue stays without any upsell. Buyers treat it as the core risk number.
Strengthen. Track churn reasons, strengthen onboarding, and intervene on at-risk accounts.
2 pts
Net revenue retention (annual) meets the benchmark
Benchmark: 110%+
Why buyers care. NRR above 100% means your customer base grows without new sales. It is the strongest proof of product value.
Strengthen. Add usage tiers or seat expansion and give customer success an expansion target.
2 pts
Monthly logo churn is at or below the benchmark
Benchmark: Under 1.5%
Why buyers care. Logo churn sets the customer lifetime, which sets LTV and the acquisition budget a buyer can justify.
Strengthen. Segment churn by plan and acquisition channel, then cut the channels that bring churn-prone customers.
1 pt
Annual or multi-year contracts cover the required share of ARR
Benchmark: 70%+ of ARR
Why buyers care. Contract term is the contractual floor under your revenue. Buyers model month-to-month revenue as at risk.
Strengthen. Offer a discount for annual prepay and renewals with auto-renew terms.
1 pt
Cohort retention is tracked by month of acquisition
Benchmark: 24 months of cohort data
Why buyers care. Cohorts show whether retention improves or decays as the product matures. A blended churn number hides this.
Strengthen. Build a monthly cohort table from billing data and keep 24 months of history.
1 pt
6

Revenue quality, continued

Expansion ARR provides the required share of ARR growth
Benchmark: 40%+ of growth
Why buyers care. Growth from existing customers is cheaper and more predictable than growth from new logos.
Strengthen. Give account management an expansion quota and track upsell by cohort.
1 pt

Unit economics

6 items
Gross margin meets the benchmark with hosting, support, and onboarding in COGS
Benchmark: 80%+
Why buyers care. Gross margin sets how much of each new dollar becomes profit. Buyers test it against the 70 to 80% SaaS norm.
Strengthen. Move support and onboarding into COGS, then cut hosting cost and automate onboarding.
1 pt
LTV to CAC ratio is tracked and meets the benchmark
Benchmark: 4x+
Why buyers care. LTV:CAC tells a buyer whether growth spend pays back. It is the efficiency number behind the growth number.
Strengthen. Compute LTV on gross profit, include commissions and onboarding in CAC, and review by channel.
2 pts
CAC payback period is at or under the benchmark
Benchmark: Under 12 months
Why buyers care. Payback sets how much cash growth consumes. Buyers with a growth plan need payback they can fund.
Strengthen. Raise prices, improve conversion, and shorten time to first value.
1 pt
Profitability meets the benchmark for your size and valuation method
Benchmark: Rule of 40 met
Why buyers care. Below $2M buyers pay on SDE. Above $5M they pay on EBITDA or on growth under the Rule of 40.
Strengthen. Audit spend by department and set a margin target that fits your growth rate.
2 pts
7

Unit economics, continued

ARR per employee meets the benchmark
Benchmark: $400K+
Why buyers care. ARR per employee is the fastest read on operating leverage. Low numbers signal a services-heavy model.
Strengthen. Automate support and onboarding and hold headcount growth below ARR growth.
1 pt
Sales and marketing spend is tracked by channel with cost per customer
Benchmark: CAC by channel for 12+ months
Why buyers care. Buyers want to know which channels work so they can add capital to them.
Strengthen. Tag every new customer with its source and compute CAC per channel quarterly.
1 pt

Customers

5 items
Customer concentration is below the benchmark
Benchmark: Top 10 under 30%
Why buyers care. One lost customer should not change the price. Buyers discount concentrated revenue or ask for an earn-out on it.
Strengthen. Diversify go-to-market and lock large accounts into multi-year contracts.
2 pts
Largest customers are on written contracts that allow assignment on a change of control
Benchmark: All customers over 1% of ARR
Why buyers care. A buyer needs the contracts to transfer. Consent clauses give customers a chance to renegotiate at close.
Strengthen. Standardize terms and amend the largest contracts before you go to market.
1 pt
Customer satisfaction is measured at least once a year (NPS or survey)
Benchmark: Quarterly survey; NPS 40+
Why buyers care. Satisfaction data predicts retention before churn shows up in the numbers.
Strengthen. Run an annual NPS survey and track the score by segment.
1 pt
Support runs on a documented process with a named owner who is not the founder
Benchmark: Support team; SLA published
Why buyers care. Support is where founder dependence shows up first. Buyers test whether customers rely on you personally.
Strengthen. Appoint a support owner, document the process, and track response time.
1 pt
8

Customers, continued

A customer success function owns renewals and expansion
Benchmark: CS lead with renewal and expansion targets
Why buyers care. At this size buyers expect a team that drives NRR, not an inbox.
Strengthen. Hire or assign a CS lead with a renewal and expansion quota.
1 pt

Owner and team

8 items
The founder can leave for the benchmark period with no drop in revenue or service
Benchmark: 3 months
Why buyers care. If the business cannot run without you, a buyer is buying a job. Transferability sets the multiple.
Strengthen. Take a planned absence, log what breaks, and fix each item.
2 pts
Sales closes without the founder at the required level
Benchmark: Sales leader and team; founder in under 10% of deals
Why buyers care. If every deal needs the founder, revenue growth is tied to the founder's hours.
Strengthen. Hire a seller, write the sales process, and move the founder out of first calls.
1 pt
A second-in-command or general manager runs day-to-day operations
Benchmark: GM or COO in place 12+ months
Why buyers care. Buyers need a leader who stays. The founder usually leaves within 12 months of a sale.
Strengthen. Promote or hire a GM and hand over operations 12 months before a sale.
1 pt
A leadership team covers product, engineering, sales, and finance
Benchmark: 4 functional leaders with 12+ months tenure
Why buyers care. At this size buyers evaluate the team as much as the numbers.
Strengthen. Fill each function with a leader who has SaaS experience.
1 pt
Key employees have employment agreements and a retention or equity plan
Benchmark: Agreements, retention plan, and option pool
Why buyers care. Buyers want the people who built the product to stay through the transition.
Strengthen. Put key people on agreements with a retention bonus that vests after close.
1 pt
An org chart shows every role and reporting line
Benchmark: Org chart current within 90 days
Why buyers care. The org chart is the buyer's map of who does what and where the founder sits.
Strengthen. Draw the chart, include contractors, and update it quarterly.
1 pt
9

Owner and team, continued

Hiring and onboarding follow a documented process
Benchmark: Hiring and onboarding process documented
Why buyers care. A buyer who plans to grow needs to hire without you.
Strengthen. Document the hiring steps and the 30-day onboarding plan for each role type.
1 pt
Operational foundations are in place: role descriptions, SOPs, 2+ people on production, productized onboarding
Benchmark: All 4 foundations in place
Why buyers care. At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
Strengthen. Audit the basics with your GM before you start a process.
1 pt

Product and technology

8 items
Architecture and operations are documented well enough for a new engineer to deploy within a week
Benchmark: Architecture doc and runbooks current
Why buyers care. Documentation is how the buyer's team takes over the codebase.
Strengthen. Write the architecture overview, the runbooks, and the environment setup guide.
1 pt
Third-party dependencies and open-source licenses are inventoried
Benchmark: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
Why buyers care. Buyers scan for copyleft licenses and unlicensed components. A finding can block a stock deal.
Strengthen. Run a license scan and resolve any copyleft or unlicensed component.
1 pt
Security meets the benchmark for your size
Benchmark: SOC 2 Type II
Why buyers care. Security findings in diligence become price reductions or indemnities.
Strengthen. Start with MFA, backups, and access control; add a penetration test and SOC 2 as you grow.
1 pt
Uptime is tracked and meets the benchmark
Benchmark: 99.95%+
Why buyers care. Reliability is a retention driver and a contractual obligation in enterprise deals.
Strengthen. Add monitoring and publish uptime to customers.
1 pt
10

Product and technology, continued

A written 12-month product roadmap exists
Benchmark: Roadmap updated within 6 months
Why buyers care. The roadmap is the buyer's view of where growth comes from after close.
Strengthen. Write a 12-month roadmap tied to retention and expansion goals.
1 pt
Differentiation is evidenced with win/loss data or documented reasons customers chose you
Benchmark: Win rate tracked; 3+ case studies
Why buyers care. Buyers pay a premium for a product that is hard to replace. Claims need evidence.
Strengthen. Track win/loss reasons in the CRM and collect 5 customer quotes on why they switched.
1 pt
Integrations or an API create switching costs
Benchmark: 3+ live integrations or a public API
Why buyers care. Switching costs protect retention and pricing. Buyers model them as a retention floor.
Strengthen. Build the 3 integrations your customers ask for most and publish an API.
1 pt
Technical foundations are in place: cloud-hosted, CI/CD, automated tests, 2+ engineers on production
Benchmark: All 4 foundations in place
Why buyers care. At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
Strengthen. Run an internal technical audit before you start a process.
1 pt

Market

5 items
The ideal customer profile is written down with segment, size, and average contract value
Benchmark: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
Why buyers care. A clear ICP lets a buyer judge the market and the growth plan. It also explains your churn.
Strengthen. Write a 1-page ICP and check that 70%+ of new customers match it.
1 pt
11

Market, continued

A bottom-up TAM and SAM exist with sources
Benchmark: TAM $500M+
Why buyers care. Buyers pay for headroom. A small or vague TAM caps the multiple even with strong metrics.
Strengthen. Build TAM from ICP count times ACV and cite the sources.
1 pt
Market growth is cited from a third-party source
Benchmark: 10%+ market growth with a cited source
Why buyers care. A growing market gives the buyer tailwind for the growth plan.
Strengthen. Cite a Gartner, Forrester, or PitchBook growth rate for your segment.
1 pt
Named competitors and your position against them are documented, with win rate
Benchmark: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate
Why buyers care. Buyers want to know who you beat and why. Win rate is the proof.
Strengthen. Keep a competitor map and track win rate against each named competitor.
1 pt
Recent acquisitions in your category are tracked
Benchmark: 10 comparable deals tracked
Why buyers care. Buyer activity in your category sets the comparable multiples.
Strengthen. Keep a list of the last 10 deals in your category with price and multiple where public.
1 pt

Legal and IP

7 items
Every employee and contractor who wrote code has signed an IP assignment
Benchmark: 100% of contributors signed
Why buyers care. Without IP assignment the company does not own its own product.
Strengthen. Audit contributors and collect signed assignments from each one.
1 pt
Trademarks are registered and all domains are owned by the company
Benchmark: Mark registered; domains in company account
Why buyers care. Brand assets must transfer with the company.
Strengthen. Register the mark and move domains into a company-owned account.
1 pt
No open litigation, claims, or regulatory issues
Benchmark: No open matters
Why buyers care. Buyers price open claims at the worst case and ask for an indemnity.
Strengthen. Settle or document every open matter before you go to market.
1 pt
12

Legal and IP, continued

Vendor and partner contracts are assignable on a change of control
Benchmark: Top 10 vendor contracts assignable
Why buyers care. Critical vendors who can terminate at close give them leverage over your deal.
Strengthen. Review the top 10 vendor contracts and amend the change-of-control clauses.
1 pt
Compliance obligations for your vertical are met (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, or others that apply)
Benchmark: Compliance map current; no open gaps
Why buyers care. Regulatory gaps are indemnity items. Enterprise buyers verify them before the LOI.
Strengthen. Map the regulations that apply and close each gap with counsel.
1 pt
A data inventory shows where customer data lives and who can access it
Benchmark: Data inventory current within 12 months
Why buyers care. Data diligence asks this question first. The answer sets the privacy risk.
Strengthen. Document every system that holds customer data and the access list for each.
1 pt
Legal foundations are in place: clean cap table, current customer terms, no open claims
Benchmark: All 3 foundations in place
Why buyers care. At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
Strengthen. Have counsel run a pre-sale legal audit.
1 pt
13
Your Score
Add the points for every box you ticked. The maximum at your stage is 64 points across 56 items.
51+Sellable at this stage. Buyers at your size will engage. Work on the next-stage items to move up the range.
32 to 50Close, with work. Fix the 2-point gaps first; they move the multiple most.
Under 32Not yet sellable at this stage. Start with Financial quality and Owner and team. Buyers stop reading when those fail.

If You Want To Sell At This Stage

Buyers at this size run a banker-led auction. Price depends on growth, NRR and the comparables in your category more than on any checklist item. The items here are the ones that keep the price intact through diligence.
